Despite Huge Final Day for Early Voting in Nashville, Turnout Still Down from 2018 by Sarah Grace Taylor, Nashville Banner October 30, 2026

Despite Huge Final Day for Early Voting in Nashville, Turnout Still Down from 2018

by Sarah Grace Taylor, Nashville Banner
October 30, 2026

Voters lined up at polling places across Nashville for the final day of early voting Thursday, in some cases waiting hours to cast their ballots. In what was by far the busiest day in more than two weeks of early voting, more than 19,000 people voted in Davidson County, easily surpassing the next busiest day and keeping polls open until 9:26 p.m., with the Southeast Library precinct in Antioch closing last. Polls closed at 7 p.m., but anyone in line at that time was entitled to vote.

But even with the late spike in activity, early numbers lag behind 2018, the last time Tennesseans had a midterm election with an open governor’s seat on the ballot. Participation is higher than the last midterm election in 2022, but still lags behind 2024 and other presidential election years. 

In total, the Davidson County Election Commission reported that 143,849 voters have cast ballots in the county, representing 29.8 percent total turnout so far. At the same point in 2018, 155,846 voters, or 36.4 percent, had participated. 

Davidson County Administrator of Elections John Richardson said Thursday's surge may be a good omen for overall turnout. 

“It’s exciting to see a strong finish to early voting,” Richardson told the Banner late Thursday. “My hope is that this momentum in early voting turnout will roll into a strong Election Day turnout.”

While the state had not updated early voting numbers on Thursday, participation was similarly down in the first 13 days compared to 2018. Through Wednesday, 1.13 million ballots had been cast statewide, down 9.95 percent from the same point in 2018. Accounting for population growth, statewide voter turnout will likely be down by a larger percentage, though 10 counties were outpacing their 2018 numbers on Wednesday. 

Overall, in 2018, Tennessee had 54.46 percent voter turnout, and Davidson County had 57.46 percent. 

Voters still have one chance to vote for U.S. Senate, Congress, governor and other statewide races and ballot measures on Tuesday, Election Day, when polls will be open from 7 a.m.-7 p.m. (CST). 

For more information on voting, candidates and issues on the ballot, visit the Banner’s voter guide.
